Carlos: Heads up 44 we had a messy handoff on the PartnerY integration test yesterday. Two different war rooms, docs scattered. can we standardize the escalation path?
Emma: Definitely. Proposal: partnerships owns channel creation + naming convention `partner-<name>-sev-YYYYMMDD` and partnership PM is the initial owner. eng-oncall is invited by default. If the incident meets internal-impact criteria, partnerships runs `/promote` which calls eng-oncall and creates a formal incident in PagerDuty.
Dina: +1 on naming. One more nuance: for hardware partners we need an ops-liaison on-call (HW-oncall) because hardware vendors often require coordination with the datacenter team. Should be listed in the channel header.
Carlos: good catch. who will maintain the runbook? we need a single source of truth pinned in the channel.
Emma: partnerships-runbooks repo will be canonical, and ops-bot will pin the relevant runbook automatically on channel creation. runbook will include: initial checklist, public comms template, contact tree, escalation rubric, and rollback checklist.
Dina: for the escalation rubric, suggest short rules: escalate to internal SEV if any of the following: 1) end-user outage >5 min across >1 region 2) customer data exposure suspected 3) failed rollback or migration 4) regulatory impact. Otherwise operate in partner-war-room mode and triage with vendor.
Carlos: QA question 44 how to handle external comms approval? partner PM drafts, then partnerships approves, legal signs off if regulatory/data, and eng PR for technical accuracy. final message originates from partner PM.
Emma: That works. Also add a `#partner-ops-rotations` channel for weekly ownership handoffs and an audit script that prints channels without owners every morning.
Dina: small UX thing 44 include a short pinned snippet with `@here` policy so people don't spam `@everyone` during war rooms.
Carlos: action items: Emma to update onboarding checklist + create PR for ops-bot pinning, Dina to draft HW-oncall cadence, I'll write the audit script.
